title: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve Brief Note
summary: A concise official profile of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve in the national tiger conservation context.
useFor: Use as a quick orientation before reading full planning, legal, and compliance documents.
researchNote: Good for high-level reserve facts, but do not treat it as a substitute for notifications, plans, or sanction records.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority, Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve brief note.

title: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve Notification
source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
summary: Official Gazette notification related to the Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve eco-sensitive zone context.
useFor: Use for legal basis, notified details, regulated activity context, and compliance interpretation.
researchNote: This is a primary legal source. Cite the Gazette notification rather than a secondary summary when making legal or policy claims.
credit: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. Gazette of India, S.O. 4268(E), 25 November 2020.

title: Mukundara Hills National Park Notification, 2012
summary: S.O. 156 of 9 January 2012 declaring Mukundara Hills National Park, after a 2006 notice of intention and rights settlement in 2009 and 2011.
useFor: Use for the legal date and basis of the national park: notice of intention 3 March 2006, rights settled in Chittorgarh (6 Aug 2009) and Kota (19 Aug 2011), final declaration under section 35(4) of the Wild Life (Protection) Act.
researchNote: The Forest Department page lists the file number as F11(56)Van/2011/Part; the scan prints F.11(56)Van/2001 Part. Quote the number as printed and give the 9 January 2012 date.
credit: Government of Rajasthan, Forest Department. Notification S.O. 156, 9 January 2012. Rajasthan Gazette Extraordinary, Part 4(C)(II), 11 January 2012.

title: Darrah Reserved Area Notification, 1955
summary: Forest Department notification of 7 November 1955 declaring Darrah, with Jaisamand, Sawai Madhopur, Sariska and Dholpur, a reserved area where hunting was banned.
useFor: Use for the history and legal origin of Darrah, the forest block most visitors know as Mukundara.
researchNote: Issued under section 5 of the Rajasthan Wild Animals and Birds Protection Act, 1951. The Forest Department web page gives the date as 01.11.1955; the Gazette notice is dated 7 November 1955.
credit: Government of Rajasthan, Forest Department. Miscellaneous No. F.39(2)For./55, 7 November 1955, Rajasthan Raj-Patra.

title: Jawahar Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary Notification, 1975
summary: S.O. 526 declaring the Kota Dam (Jawahar Sagar) reservoir on the Chambal and its surrounding forests a wildlife sanctuary to protect gharial and mugger, with boundary description.
useFor: Use for the legal origin of the Chambal gorge sanctuary between Kota and Rawatbhata.
researchNote: Issued under section 18 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 by the Revenue (Group-VIII) Department. The Forest Department page prints the date as 09.10.19 followed by 75.
credit: Government of Rajasthan, Revenue (Group-VIII) Department. Notification S.O. 526, 9 October 1975, No. F.3(5)(13)Rev/8/73, Rajasthan Raj-Patra.

title: National Chambal (Gharial) Sanctuary Notifications, 1979 and 1983
summary: The 1979 order declaring the National Gharial Sanctuary on the Chambal below Jawahar Sagar dam, and the 3 September 1983 Gazette notification of the sanctuary.
useFor: Use for the legal basis of the Chambal river stretch in the reserve core and its gharial protection.
researchNote: Both use file No. F.11(12)Rev/8/78. The 1979 order describes a 100 m strip on each bank; the 1983 Gazette text describes a 1,000 m strip. The day of the 1979 order is handwritten and hard to read; the Forest Department page gives 07.12.1979.
credit: Government of Rajasthan, Revenue Department. Notification No. F.11(12)Rev/8/78 (1979) and Rajasthan Raj-Patra notification of 3 September 1983.
seoTitle: National Chambal Sanctuary Notifications, Rajasthan, 1979 and 1983

title: Bhainsrorgarh Wildlife Sanctuary Notification, 1983
summary: Original notification of Bhainsrorgarh Sanctuary in Chittorgarh district, whose forests were added to the tiger reserve core in October 2023.
useFor: Use with the 5 October 2023 amending notification to trace where the newer part of the core comes from.
researchNote: Spelt Bhainsrodgarh, Bhensrodgarh and Baisorgarh in different official files; all refer to the same sanctuary.
credit: Government of Rajasthan. Notification No. F.11(44)Rev/8/81, 5 February 1983, Rajasthan Raj-Patra, 17 February 1983.

title: Tiger Conservation Plan - Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve (Earlier Archive)
source: WII MEE-TR portal / Rajasthan Forest Department
summary: Earlier archived long-form planning document for reserve management, protection, habitat, prey, tourism, eco-development, and monitoring priorities.
useFor: Use for management background. For the current legal area (1,135.787 sq km since 5 October 2023) use the 2023 amending notification.
researchNote: Useful for management questions, but it predates the 5 October 2023 notification that added Bhainsrodgarh-area forests to the core.
credit: Source: Rajasthan Forest Department, Tiger Conservation Plan of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, 2020-21 to 2029-30 (copy from the WII MEE-TR portal).

title: Tiger Conservation Plan - MHTR with Bhainsrodgarh Core Addition
type: Core management plan / updated official copy
source: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve / Rajasthan Forest Department
summary: Newer official TCP archive that states Bhainsrodgarh Sanctuary was added to Mukandra Hills Tiger Reserve by order 4854336 dated 05.10.2023 and made part of the core tiger reserve.
useFor: Use for the current Bhainsrodgarh core-addition context, updated management framing, corridor notes, protection infrastructure and long-form planning details.
researchNote: This is the key source for the Bhainsrodgarh update. It is large; open in a dedicated tab when reading maps, annexures or tables.
credit: Source: Rajasthan Forest Department, Tiger Conservation Plan of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve (updated copy).

title: Annual Plan of Operation 2019-20 - MHTR
summary: Operational and financial planning record for Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve for the 2019-20 cycle.
useFor: Use for budget heads, approved actions, implementation priorities, and annual management intent.
researchNote: Compare APO line items with field outcomes and later sanction documents to understand continuity or gaps.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority, APO sanction for Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, 2019-20.

title: NTCA APO Sanction - Mukundra Tiger Reserve 2022-23
summary: NTCA approval of the 2022-23 Annual Plan of Operation for MHTR: APO cost Rs 615.30 lakh, central share Rs 350.19 lakh, with release held back against an unspent balance.
useFor: Use to fill the gap between the 2019-20 APO and the 2024-25 and 2025-26 sanctions.
researchNote: Approval does not prove expenditure or completion; check utilisation certificates and later sanctions.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority, F. No. 4-1(43)/2022-PT, 12 December 2022.

title: NTCA Sanction Order - Rajasthan 2024
summary: Recent NTCA sanction document for tiger reserve work in Rajasthan, useful for tracking funded priorities and current-cycle conservation support.
useFor: Use to understand sanctioned priorities, funding direction, and current-cycle management support.
researchNote: Read alongside reserve-specific APOs and implementation reports; sanction does not by itself prove field completion.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority, sanction order for Rajasthan tiger reserves, 2024-25 (first instalment).

title: Management Effectiveness Evaluation Technical Manual - Tiger Reserves in India
summary: NTCA technical manual explaining the Management Effectiveness Evaluation framework used for tiger reserves in India.
useFor: Use for understanding MEE terminology, evaluation criteria, management-effectiveness context and how tiger reserves are assessed.
researchNote: This is not MHTR-specific, but it helps readers understand official management evaluation language used across tiger reserves.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority, MEE Technical Manual, 2022.

title: Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves in India, 2018 (4th cycle)
source: National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: The fourth national MEE cycle, with the reserve-wise score and evaluators’ notes for Mukundara Hills before tigers were brought back.
useFor: Use to compare MHTR’s 2018 assessment with the 2022 cycle.
researchNote: Scores are not strictly comparable across cycles because the framework changed; compare the evaluators’ notes as well as the numbers. The file is over 100 MB, so it is linked rather than hosted.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India, Fourth cycle of MEE of Tiger Reserves in India, 2018.

title: Assessment of Cheetah Introduction Sites and Proposed Actions (Technical Note)
source: Wildlife Institute of India with Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh Forest Departments
summary: Field assessment of candidate cheetah sites, including a survey of Mukundara on 22-23 November 2020: the 80 sq km enclosure, prey densities and the conclusion that the reserve was not then ready.
useFor: Use for 2020 prey density figures, the enclosure, and the management actions WII listed for MHTR.
researchNote: A short rapid survey; treat the prey densities as indicative. Reserve area is the pre-2023 figure of 759 sq km.
credit: Jhala, Y.V., Bipin, C.M., Jhala, H.Y., Yadav, S.R. and Chauhan, J.S. (2021). Assessment of cheetah introduction sites and proposed actions: technical note. Wildlife Institute of India, Forest Department of Rajasthan and Forest Department of Madhya Pradesh.

title: Reintroduction and Population Recovery of Tigers in India: Field Experiences and Key Learnings
source: NTCA and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: Case studies of tiger reintroductions, including Mukundara: translocation from Ranthambhore from 2018, an 82 sq km enclosure, mortality setbacks and 7 tigers present.
useFor: Use for the official account of the reintroduction and what NTCA and WII say limits recovery here.
researchNote: The report is marked all rights reserved, so it is linked, not hosted.
credit: NTCA-WII (2026). Reintroduction and Population Recovery of Tigers in India: Field Experiences and Key Learnings. National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India.
seoTitle: Tiger Reintroduction in India: NTCA-WII Field Learnings 2026

title: Zonal Master Plan for Eco-sensitive Zone of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: Zonal planning document for the eco-sensitive zone context around Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve.
useFor: Use for zoning logic, permissible activity interpretation, land-use compatibility, and planning controls.
researchNote: Important for development-pressure analysis around the reserve; pair with legal notifications and local planning records.
credit: Source: Department of Environment and Climate Change, Government of Rajasthan, Zonal Master Plan for the MHTR eco-sensitive zone, 7 December 2023.

title: Notified ESZ Document - Rajasthan Tiger Reserve Section
summary: A compact Rajasthan Forest Department PDF covering ESZ and tiger reserve reference tables, including Mukundara.
useFor: Use for quick ESZ and reserve-area reference across Rajasthan tiger reserves.
researchNote: Useful as a compact table source, but cite full notifications and ZMP documents for detailed compliance work.
credit: Source: Rajasthan Forest Department, notified eco-sensitive zones table.

title: Bhainsrorgarh Wildlife Sanctuary Eco-sensitive Zone Notification, 2021
source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
summary: Final notification of the eco-sensitive zone around Bhainsrorgarh Sanctuary, the second ESZ in the reserve’s outer boundary.
useFor: Use with the 2020 MHTR ESZ notification for rules on activities around the Bhainsrorgarh part of the core.
researchNote: The ESZ was drawn around the sanctuary before it joined the tiger reserve in 2023; see the boundaries page for where the two ESZs meet.
credit: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. S.O. 3683(E), 10 September 2021. Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3(ii), No. 3371, 13 September 2021.

title: Wildlife Clearance File - Bharatmala NH-148N Section near MHTR
summary: Wildlife conservation / clearance file for a highway section in the wider Mukundara-Darrah landscape context.
useFor: Use for mitigation commitments, project conditions, and wildlife-clearance context around infrastructure proposals.
researchNote: The conditions and mitigation sections are critical; they define obligations after approval.
credit: Submitted by the National Highways Authority of India; published on the Government of India environment clearance portal, 14 November 2019.

title: Reptiles and Amphibians of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: A field guide-style reference focused on reptiles and amphibians recorded in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve.
useFor: Use for non-mammal baseline context, field identification support, and biodiversity education.
researchNote: A useful counterweight to tiger-only narratives; verify taxonomy against current sources when needed.
credit: Source: Wildlife Institute of India and Rajasthan Forest Department (Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve), Amphibians and Reptiles of MHTR.

title: A Preliminary Bird Guide of Mukandra Hills Tiger Reserve
source: Wildlife Institute of India and Rajasthan Forest Department
summary: Illustrated guide to 219 bird species recorded in the reserve, with protection schedule, IUCN status, guild, migratory status and habitat for each.
useFor: Use for species identification, an official bird checklist, and the Chambal gorge Indian vulture colony context.
researchNote: A preliminary guide, so absence from it does not mean a species is absent. Check names against current taxonomy before reuse.
credit: Sai, A. and Das, A. (2025). A Preliminary Bird Guide of Mukandra Hills Tiger Reserve. Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, and Mukandra Hills Tiger Reserve, Rajasthan Forest Department.

title: Phytodiversity Characterization of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
source: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
summary: Research article on plant diversity characterization in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve.
useFor: Use for sampling design, plant diversity records, and habitat interpretation.
researchNote: Review methods and sampling effort before using headline diversity claims.
credit: Dharmendra Kumar et al. (2020). Phytodiversity Characterization of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve. International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences 9(7). Open access, Creative Commons licence.

title: Status of Wildlife between Kota Barrage and Jawahar Sagar Dam, Rajasthan
summary: A WII rapid assessment report on aquatic wildlife and river habitat quality along the Chambal River stretch between Kota Barrage and Jawahar Sagar Dam.
useFor: Use for Chambal river-valley context, otter signs, crocodile and turtle records, waterbirds, raptors, fish diversity, and development-impact interpretation around the wider Mukundara landscape.
researchNote: This report can contain sensitive field locations. Use it for ecological context and citation, but avoid republishing precise nest, roost, or wildlife-use coordinates.
credit: Johnson, J.A., George, A., Sharma, M., Kavin, D., Suresh, S., Gopi, G.V. and Hussain, S.A. (2021). Status of wildlife between Kota barrage and Jawahar Sagar Dam, Rajasthan. Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun.

title: Caracal Comeback in Ramgarh Visdhari and Mukundara Hills
summary: Open-access natural history note documenting the first photographic record of caracal from Ramgarh Visdhari and Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserves.
useFor: Use for caracal distribution, rare small-cat conservation context, camera-trap monitoring value and semi-arid western Indian landscape interpretation.
researchNote: The article includes camera-trap maps and record context. Cite the finding without republishing precise wildlife-use locations.
credit: Thakar, R. et al. (2025). Caracal’s Comeback: first photographic record of caracal in the Ramgarh Visdhari and Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, India. Journal of Wildlife Science 2(3): 100-103. doi:10.63033/JWLS.IFNA7720. CC BY 4.0.

title: Record of Cinereous Vulture from Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: Short communication reporting a Cinereous Vulture sighting from Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve during a February-March 2015 prey-status study.
useFor: Use for vulture occurrence, scavenger records, raptor context, and evidence that MHTR supports more than tiger-focused conservation values.
researchNote: The article includes field context and a precise observation locality. Cite the record, but avoid amplifying sensitive location detail unnecessarily.
credit: Vulture News 71 (2016). doi:10.4314/vulnew.v71i1.4.

title: Occupancy and Habitat Use of Sloth Bear in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: Study of sloth bear occupancy, signs, den records and habitat use in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, with mixed forest and water-adjacent habitats highlighted.
useFor: Use for sloth bear distribution, habitat preference, sign-survey context and human-use pressure around MHTR.
researchNote: The paper discusses bear signs and den habitat. Use the ecological findings carefully and avoid turning site-specific records into visitor guidance.
credit: Sultana, F., Khan, S. and Nabi, G. (2015). Occupancy and habitat use of sloth bear in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve. Flora and Fauna 21(2): 203-208.

title: Sloth Bear Diet in Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve
source: International Journal of Research and Analytical Reviews
summary: Research article on sloth bear food availability and scat-based diet composition in Darrah Wildlife Sanctuary, part of the Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve landscape.
useFor: Use for sloth bear feeding ecology, seasonal food context, plant-food references and insect-heavy diet interpretation.
researchNote: Treat the percentages as study-specific results from sampled scats, not as a complete diet profile for every season or part of the reserve.
credit: Khan, S. and Sultana, F. (2022). Food availability and dietary composition of sloth bear in Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve. International Journal of Research and Analytical Reviews 9(3).

title: Dietary Composition of Leopard in Mukandara Hills National Park
source: International Journal of Pure and Applied Bioscience
summary: Scat-analysis study of leopard diet in Mukandara Hills National Park, recording prey items such as Hanuman langur, jackal, nilgai, fox, wild boar and domestic dog.
useFor: Use for leopard prey context, historical carnivore ecology and comparing prey-base notes with later MHTR management documents.
researchNote: The paper uses an older protected-area name and a small scat sample. Cross-check with newer monitoring data before making broad prey-base claims.
credit: Meena, H.M., Lal, G., Kumar, S. and Nama, K.S. (2013). Dietary composition of leopard in Mukandara Hills National Park. International Journal of Pure and Applied Bioscience 1(6): 72-76.

title: Kali Sindh River - Vibrant Ganga Biodiversity Brief
source: Wildlife Institute of India / Ganga Knowledge Portal
summary: A river-basin brief for the Kali Sindh, including land-cover, river-system and biodiversity context for the basin that passes through Darrah Wildlife Sanctuary in MHTR.
useFor: Use for Kali Sindh basin context, riverine biodiversity, fishing cat and otter habitat references, and wider Chambal-linked landscape interpretation.
researchNote: This is a concise brochure, not a full technical report. Pair it with detailed river, wetland and protected-area studies for analysis.
credit: Source: Wildlife Institute of India and National Mission for Clean Ganga, Kali Sindh river brochure (copy from the Ganga Knowledge Portal).

title: Wildlife Corridors of Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve
source: International Journal of Education, Modern Management, Applied Science & Social Science
summary: Research paper focused on wildlife-corridor significance for Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve and wider biodiversity conservation.
useFor: Use as a secondary corridor-context source, especially when discussing connectivity, gene flow, landscape permeability and conservation planning.
researchNote: Treat as a research reference rather than a legal or management notification. Cross-check corridor claims against official plans and GIS sources.
credit: Bairwa, M.K., Kalia, S., Gardner, J. and Saraswat, A. (2023). Wildlife corridors of Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve. IJEMMASSS 5(2-III): 92-107.

title: Vertebrate Fauna of the Chambal River Basin, with Emphasis on the National Chambal Sanctuary
summary: Basin-wide checklist of 147 fish, 56 reptile, 308 bird and 60 mammal species, covering the Jawahar Sagar to Kota stretch of the Chambal.
useFor: Use for river and gorge fauna of the Chambal stretch that runs through the reserve core.
researchNote: Records are basin-wide, not by stretch, so do not use it to claim a species for MHTR specifically.
credit: Nair, T. and Krishna, Y.C. (2013). Vertebrate fauna of the Chambal River Basin, with emphasis on the National Chambal Sanctuary, India. Journal of Threatened Taxa 5(2): 3620-3641. doi:10.11609/JoTT.o3238.3620-41. CC BY 3.0.
seoTitle: Vertebrate Fauna of the Chambal River Basin (JoTT 2013)

title: Abundance and Activity of Carnivores in Two Protected Areas of Semi-arid Western India
summary: WII camera-trap comparison of carnivore abundance and activity in Ranthambhore and in Mukundara before tigers re-established.
useFor: Use for leopard, hyena, jackal and other carnivore patterns in MHTR under high human pressure.
researchNote: Publisher-copyrighted; read through the DOI or ask the authors for a copy.
credit: Latafat, K., Sadhu, A., Qureshi, Q. and Jhala, Y.V. (2023). Abundance and activity of carnivores in two protected areas of semi-arid western India with varying top predator density and human impacts. European Journal of Wildlife Research 69: 15.
seoTitle: Carnivores of Ranthambhore and Mukundara (2023 study)

title: Ethnomedicinal Studies on Ferns and Fern Allies of Hadoti Plateau, South-eastern Rajasthan
summary: Short note on eleven fern species and their medicinal use by Sahariya, Bhil and Kanjar communities in the Hadoti region, including the Mukundara hill ranges.
useFor: Use for ethnobotany and lower-plant records in the wider Mukundara landscape.
researchNote: Regional, not reserve-specific; uses traditional knowledge that should be credited to the communities named.
credit: Sharma, N.K. (2002). Ethnomedicinal studies on ferns and fern allies of Hadoti Plateau, south-eastern Rajasthan. Zoos' Print Journal 17(3): 732-734.
seoTitle: Ethnomedicinal Ferns of the Hadoti Plateau (2002)

title: Lok Sabha Answer - Genetic Inbreeding in Tiger Sub-Populations
summary: Government answer on tiger sub-population inbreeding, connectivity, Project Tiger implementation and corridors involving Ranthambore, Kuno, Madhav and Mukundra.
useFor: Use for official parliamentary wording on tiger connectivity, genetic-inbreeding concerns and inter-reserve corridor policy context.
researchNote: This is a policy-answer source. Use scientific studies and corridor assessments alongside it for ecological interpretation.
credit: Source: Lok Sabha Secretariat, Unstarred Question 473, answered 6 February 2023 (Digital Library of Parliament).

title: Status of Tigers, Co-predators and Prey in India 2022
source: NTCA and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: National tiger-estimation report covering tiger status, landscapes, co-predators, prey, habitat connectivity, camera-trapped sites and conservation implications.
useFor: Use for national and landscape-scale context around tiger monitoring, co-predator/prey assessment and connectivity framing relevant to MHTR.
researchNote: This is broad national context and includes sensitive survey information. Use it for interpretation, but avoid extracting precise camera or wildlife-use locations.
credit: Qureshi, Q., Jhala, Y.V., Yadav, S.P. and Mallick, A. (eds.) (2023). Status of Tigers, Co-predators and Prey in India, 2022. National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India.

title: Status of Tigers, Co-predators and Prey in India, 2018
source: NTCA and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: National tiger estimation report for the 2018 cycle, the year tigers were first released into Mukundara.
useFor: Use as the baseline for the 2022 report when describing the reserve and the Ranthambhore-Mukundara landscape.
researchNote: National report with sensitive survey detail; do not extract camera or wildlife-use locations. The file is over 100 MB, so it is linked rather than hosted.
credit: Jhala, Y.V., Qureshi, Q. and Nayak, A.K. (eds.) (2020). Status of Tigers, Co-predators and Prey in India, 2018. National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India.

title: An Illustrative Profile of Tiger Reserves of India
source: WII EIACP Programme Centre and National Tiger Conservation Authority
summary: Illustrated profile of every tiger reserve; the Mukundara page covers its hill ridges, the four protected areas in the core and links to Ranthambhore.
useFor: Use for the official short profile alongside the NTCA brief note.
researchNote: The Mukundara page predates the 2023 Bhainsrorgarh addition; check area figures against the 5 October 2023 notification.
credit: Nautiyal, J.P., Lone, A.M., Ghosh, T., Malick, A., Yadav, S.P., Ramesh, C. and Ramesh, K. (2023). An Illustrative Profile of Tiger Reserves of India. EIACP Programme Centre, Wildlife Institute of India, and National Tiger Conservation Authority.

title: Global Tiger Protected Area Compendium
summary: Large comparative compendium for tiger protected areas across the tiger range.
useFor: Use for broad comparative framing against other tiger landscapes.
researchNote: Informative for context, not a replacement for Mukundara-specific planning records.
credit: Global Tiger Forum (2021). Global Tiger Protected Area Compendium.

title: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve Notification, 2013
summary: The base Rajasthan notification declaring 417.17188 sq km as Critical Tiger Habitat and 342.82274 sq km as buffer, totalling 759.99462 sq km.
useFor: Use as the historical legal baseline for MHTR core, buffer and total area before the 2023 amendment.
researchNote: The filename mentions ESZ, but the document is the 2013 tiger-reserve notification. Read it separately from the final 2020 ESZ Gazette.
credit: Government of Rajasthan, Forest Department. Notification of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, 9 April 2013 (Rajasthan Gazette, 18 April 2013).

title: MHTR Core and Buffer Amending Notification, 2023
summary: The amendment revising MHTR to 690.71178 sq km of Critical Tiger Habitat and 445.07522 sq km of buffer, totalling 1,135.787 sq km.
useFor: Use for the current state-government legal area and the Bhainsrodgarh core-addition context.
researchNote: The Forest Department link currently exposes a one-page scan whose table continues beyond the visible page. Use the published area figures with the current protected-area register and updated Tiger Conservation Plan; do not infer an unseen full schedule.
credit: Government of Rajasthan, Forest Department. Amending notification for Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, 5 October 2023.

title: Rajasthan Long Term Action Plan for Tiger Conservation
issued: Approved 6 Oct 2023; maps updated through Oct 2023
summary: Statewide tiger-conservation action plan that records an in-principle proposal for further MHTR core and buffer additions and sets out conditions before notification.
useFor: Use for proposal status, connectivity and management priorities; keep proposed additions separate from the notified reserve area.
researchNote: The MHTR proposal is not itself a boundary notification. The plan records further consent, State approval and statutory steps.
credit: Source: Rajasthan Forest Department, Long-term Action Plan for Tiger Conservation in Rajasthan, 2023.

title: Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves in India, 2022 — Fifth Cycle
source: National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: The fifth-cycle national MEE report, including MHTR's 60.16 percent score, Good rating and dated management observations.
useFor: Use for the conditions documented during the 2022 evaluation, management strengths, recommendations and comparable national methodology.
researchNote: The observations are a dated evaluation, not a live statement of conditions in 2026. Later evidence should be checked for each issue.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India, Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves in India, 5th cycle (2022), report 2023.

title: NTCA Rajasthan Annual Plan Sanction, 2025–26
summary: Rajasthan's FY2025–26 tiger-reserve approval and first-instalment sanction, including the MHTR programme and release calculation.
useFor: Use for approved budget heads and management intent in FY2025–26.
researchNote: Approval or fund release does not prove expenditure, completion or ecological outcome; follow-up evidence is required.
credit: Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority, APO sanction for Rajasthan tiger reserves, 2025-26.

title: CAG Chapter IV: Management of Tiger Reserves in Rajasthan
source: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
summary: Subject Specific Compliance Audit chapter on Rajasthan tiger-reserve management for FY2016–17 to FY2020–21, with later position updates identified in the report.
useFor: Use for dated, system-level accountability themes such as staffing, protection, invasive species, land security, relocation and participation.
researchNote: Do not assign statewide or multi-reserve findings to MHTR alone, and do not present historical audit findings as verified current conditions.
credit: Source: Comptroller and Auditor General of India, Report No. 5 of 2025, Government of Rajasthan, Chapter IV (forest).

title: Rajasthan Human–Wildlife Conflict Ex-Gratia Order, 2026
summary: State order revising ex-gratia amounts and procedure for human death, permanent incapacity and injury caused by wildlife.
useFor: Use for current compensation amounts, eligibility conditions and process; verify the live Forest Department record before filing a claim.
researchNote: The order sets ₹10 lakh for death or permanent incapacity, ₹2 lakh for grievous injury and ₹25,000 for minor injury, subject to its certification and procedural conditions.
credit: Source: Rajasthan Forest Department, ex-gratia order for wildlife-caused death and injury, 2026.

title: Rajasthan Voluntary Village Relocation Package Amendment, 2025
summary: Order replacing the 2022 land-package provisions and confirming a choice between the prescribed land package and ₹15 lakh cash—or the then-applicable NTCA amount—per displaced family.
useFor: Use for current package options while assessing consent, rights settlement, eligibility, land, services and livelihood outcomes.
researchNote: Relocation from protected areas must be described as voluntary and rights-based; a package announcement is not evidence of consent or completed rehabilitation.
credit: Source: Government of Rajasthan, Forest Department, order of 24 July 2025 modifying the village relocation land package.

title: Progress of Village Relocation in Rajasthan Tiger Reserves (March 2024)
summary: Tiger reserve areas and village relocation in Rajasthan; for Mukundara Hills, 14 core villages to relocate, 2 relocated and 2 in progress.
useFor: Use for the official relocation status before the 2025 package change.
researchNote: Uses the pre-2023 area (759.99 sq km), before the Bhainsrorgarh addition. Treat counts as the department’s statement at that date, not as evidence of consent or rehabilitation outcomes.
credit: Source: Rajasthan Forest Department, progress of relocation in tiger reserves, as on March 2024.
